svg.title: Collection Yield by Acquisition Sub-Niche
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-04-subniche-collection-yields; chart type: horizontal_bars; title: Collection Yield by Acquisition Sub-Niche; subtitle: Illustrative dollars banked within 30 days per $100 invoiced.; chapter number: 2; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Five independent underwriting examples use hypothetical collection assumptions, not observed sector averages. Numeric values are percentages of an invoice cohort collected within 30 days. Collections are measured before payment-processing fees; slower collection does not automatically mean bad debt.; caption: Compare cash conversion rather than mistaking payment-rail receipts for incremental sales or owner profit. Replace every assumption with target-specific invoice and bank evidence.; stages: label: Managed IT services; value: $95 banked per $100 invoiced; numeric value: 95.0; detail: Illustrative recurring ACH cohort: verify debit authorizations, return histories, disputed service credits, and whether customer contracts survive the ownership change.; label: Commercial cleaning; value: $90 banked per $100 invoiced; numeric value: 90.0; detail: Illustrative ACH and check cohort: inspect customer payment runs, site acceptance requirements, invoice disputes, and payroll funded before customer collection.; label: Equipment maintenance; value: $85 banked per $100 invoiced; numeric value: 85.0; detail: Illustrative card and ACH cohort: reconcile signed service tickets, parts charges, processor deductions, refund exposure, and commercial-account credit terms.; label: Specialty distribution; value: $80 banked per $100 invoiced; numeric value: 80.0; detail: Illustrative trade-credit cohort: test delivery evidence, returns, deductions, inventory funding, and customer credit limits rather than relying on invoice totals.; label: Commercial field services; value: $75 banked per $100 invoiced; numeric value: 75.0; detail: Illustrative milestone-billing cohort: identify retainage, purchase-order mismatches, disputed completion certificates, and collection delays hidden inside reported receivables.

circle.title: label: Managed IT services; value: $95 banked per $100 invoiced; numeric value: 95.0; detail: Illustrative recurring ACH cohort: verify debit authorizations, return histories, disputed service credits, and whether customer contracts survive the ownership change.

label: Commercial cleaning; value: $90 banked per $100 invoiced; numeric value: 90.0; detail: Illustrative ACH and check cohort: inspect customer payment runs, site acceptance requirements, invoice disputes, and payroll funded before customer collection.

label: Equipment maintenance; value: $85 banked per $100 invoiced; numeric value: 85.0; detail: Illustrative card and ACH cohort: reconcile signed service tickets, parts charges, processor deductions, refund exposure, and commercial-account credit terms.

label: Specialty distribution; value: $80 banked per $100 invoiced; numeric value: 80.0; detail: Illustrative trade-credit cohort: test delivery evidence, returns, deductions, inventory funding, and customer credit limits rather than relying on invoice totals.

label: Commercial field services; value: $75 banked per $100 invoiced; numeric value: 75.0; detail: Illustrative milestone-billing cohort: identify retainage, purchase-order mismatches, disputed completion certificates, and collection delays hidden inside reported receivables.

text.title: Assumptions: Five independent underwriting examples use hypothetical collection assumptions, not observed sector averages. Numeric values are percentages of an invoice cohort collected within 30 days. Collections are measured before payment-processing fees; slower collection does not automatically mean bad debt.
